sources: Smithsonian's National Zoo, Komodo dragon: wild adults about 154 lb; largest verified 10.3 ft and 366 lb; venom gland in the lower jaw, venom prevents clotting, causing massive blood loss and shock; can eat up to 80% of its body weight in one meal; smell is its main food detector, sampled with a forked tongue; runs briefly 10-13 mph but hunts by stealth and power; only on a few Indonesian islands (Komodo, Rintja, Padar, Flores); https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/komodo-dragon

Fry et al. 2009, PNAS 106(22): 8969-8974: Komodo skull poorly adapted to high bite force but resists pulling loads; rejects the toxic-bacteria idea; venom causes anticoagulation and shock; https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0810883106

Watts et al. 2006, Nature 444: 1021-1022, Parthenogenesis in Komodo dragons: genetic fingerprinting showed offspring of two zoo females kept away from males had no father; https://doi.org/10.1038/4441021a

beats.say: A lizard ten feet long is tasting the air for you, with its forked tongue.
Its bite has venom that stops your blood from clotting.
The Komodo dragon. About a hundred fifty pounds, in the wild.
It can run ten to thirteen miles an hour, in short bursts.
It can eat up to eighty percent of its own weight, in one meal.
People said its dirty mouth germs killed its prey. Scientists say it's the venom.
Would Meatball survive? Only if he stays home. It lives on just a few islands in Indonesia.
